title: Shift squares for primitive strict-system structural comparisons
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$ and uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$. On small pro-etale sites of finite-type $k$-schemes let $\mathscr S_W$ be strict semilinear systems of $(A_n)_W$-module sheaves, with system inverse image $P_v$, total derived direct image $S_v$, exact open extension $J_j$, and derived system tensor, realized on the simultaneous ringed diagram sites of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]. Maps $v$ are separated finite type and opens $j$ are quasi-compact. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories of these module systems. Give these functors the cochain-shift comparisons of [lem-pur-integral-basic-operation-shift]; tensor uses the signed total comparison $t_{a,b}:M[a]\otimes^LN[b]\cong(M\otimes^LN)[a+b]$ with coefficient $(-1)^{bp}$ on $M[a]^p\otimes N[b]^q$ [lem-pur-shifted-tensor-morphism-calculus].

Each of the following primitive natural transformations commutes with every integer shift in each designated input occurrence: the canonical system pullback compositors and square identifications induced by equality of scheme composites; the pullback/tensor comparisons; the tensor associator, unitors and Koszul symmetry; open-extension composition; and, for open immersions $b:V_W\to V$ and $s:U\to V_W$ with $k=bs$, the canonical restriction identification $P_bJ_k\cong J_s$. If $s$ is also closed, the canonical clopen comparison $J_s\cong S_s$ and the component projection $\pi_s:1\to J_sP_s$ (identity on $s(U)$, zero on its open complement) also commute with all these shifts, in the normalization of [lem-sf-semilinear-proper-open-mate-pasting]. Precisely, if $\tau:F\to G$ is any listed map and one input $M$ is replaced by $M[r]$, its canonical comparisons satisfy $\chi_G\circ\tau_{M[r]}=\tau_M[r]\circ\chi_F$; for symmetry the shifted occurrence is followed to its permuted position. These are identities of semilinear-system transformations before evaluation or scalar restriction. No integral realization, arbitrary expression-tree comparison, proper/open mate, or projection/exchange transformation is asserted.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-diagram-pullback-monoidal-shift-models] to $C_n=R/t^n$ on the small pro-etale ringed diagrams in the statement. Its termwise pullbacks, K-flat tensor and specified comparisons are the ones fixed here: [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization] defines the system pullback compositors and tensor/pullback maps as the derived classes of the canonical maps on flat-term K-flat system resolutions, and the shift comparisons of [lem-pur-integral-basic-operation-shift] are the termwise and K-flat shifts of those ringed-diagram models, with the signed tensor comparison $t_{a,b}$ of [lem-pur-shifted-tensor-morphism-calculus]. The compositor and equal-composite formulas give the pullback squares. Its bidegree formula gives the pullback/tensor squares, and its associator and unitor formulas give all their input slots. In its symmetry formula put $a=r,b=0$, or $a=0,b=r$: the scalar $(-1)^{ab}$ is $1$, giving precisely the required square with the shifted occurrence in its permuted slot.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-diagram-open-clopen-shift-models] to the same coefficient system and to the given $b,s,k=bs$. Its open-unit normalization is exactly the fixed normalization here: the system open maps of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization] are normalized by [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], their open extension and direct-image shifts in [lem-pur-integral-basic-operation-shift] are the termwise and K-injective ones, and its clopen comparison and projection are those of [lem-sf-semilinear-proper-open-mate-pasting], as the model lemma states. The termwise transitivity and restriction comparisons give the open composition and $P_bJ_k\cong J_s$ squares. When $s$ is closed, its product decomposition identifies the canonical $J_s\cong S_s$ and the specified projection with the maps in this statement; the asserted comparison uses the same K-injective/mate shift, so its last shift equations give both remaining squares.

proof.text: Both cited model lemmas assert these equations intrinsically before evaluation or scalar restriction, and supply naturality and addition of shifts. Thus each preceding square is an equality of the required semilinear-system transformations. Composing two such equations cancels the intermediate shift comparison; whiskering preserves equality and uses the specified functor shift comparison. This proves the asserted compatibility without introducing any further primitive transformation.
